notes:
Customer snapshot and key context:
- Company: mid-market analytics SaaS (product telemetry + help-center search).
- Current stack: front-end search on Pinecone (prod), Airflow for batch ETL, OpenSearch for metadata.
- Why Redwood: interested in unified hosted -> dedicated path; wants the same SDK & rollouts across environments.
- Primary asks: high-throughput embedding generation for nightly batches + low-latency live embeddings for near-real-time document ingestion. Specific targets: ~150 embeddings/sec sustained for live ingestion, nightly batches of up to 1M docs over a 6-8 hour window, and vector DB integration to replace Pinecone or run alongside it.
- Latency/throughput goals: embedding latency target < 100ms per request for small batch calls (1-16 items), cost sensitivity target <$0.0005 per embedding to beat current OpenAI+Pinecone economics.
- Model preferences: prefers open/quantized variants (smaller footprint models) for Dedicated but will test Redwood-verified embeddings in Hosted. Looking for recommendations from Redwood Optimize on quantization and batching config.
- Security: must support SSO/SAML, SOC2 + audit logs, KMS integration; legal raised data residency requirement for EU customers.
- Integration notes: wants out-of-the-box connectors to Pinecone/Weaviate/Redis; they run Airflow + Spark for preprocessing and expect a straightforward batch API or SDK call to push vector files.
- Quote from CTO: "If Dedicated can demonstrate stable cost and hit our nightly throughput numbers, we'll commit to 6 months. Otherwise we'll stay with current Pinecone flow."
- Pricing sensitivity: a hard internal threshold — price per embedding + vector storage must reduce total monthly vector infra cost by ~20% vs current.
- POC ask: 1-week Dedicated node for benchmark (1M nightly ingestion), Redwood to provide sample workbooks for batch tuning, and a short security questionnaire response for legal.
- Internal champions: Head of Product (evaluation lead), Data Engineering (owns Airflow), CTO (final sign-off).
- Selling motions so far: AE-led demo -> SE deep dive -> ops pricing -> legal.
- Risk: if Redwood cannot show clear drop in unit cost or provide residency assurances, they pivot back to Pinecone + OpenAI embeddings.
sal_summary: Mid-market SaaS evaluating Hosted then Dedicated. Good technical fit; main decision drivers are throughput benchmarks for large nightly batches, vector DB compatibility, and cost per-embed. SE recommends dedicated POC and Optimize run to tune batching+cache.
